body.p: Claims 1, 5, 10, 14, 18, and 20 are amended. Accordingly, upon entry of this
amendment, claims 1-20 will remain pending. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration in view of the remarks presented below.
Claims 1-3, 5-12, and 14-20 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as allegedly being

unpatentable over Weinert U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2007/0179434 (hereinafter, "Weinert") in view of Thukral U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2009/006061 (hereinafter, "Thukral"). Claims 4 and 13 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Weinert and Thukral, and further in view of Mazlish U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2018/0200439 (hereinafter, "Mazlish").

Without conceding in the basis of the rejections, and solely to expedite prosecution of this Application, independent claims 1, 10, and 18 have been amended to recite, inter alia: obtaining an estimated protein value for a meal and an estimated carbohydrate value for the meal;

p.u: converting the estimated protein value into a corresponding carbohydrate value by applying the estimated
protein value to a mathematical function or by dividing the

body.p: estimated protein value by a conversion factor; [and]
determining an equivalent carbohydrate value for the meal by adding the estimated carbohydrate value for the meal to the

p.u: corresponding carbohydrate value associated with the

body.p: (Claim 1 as amended; claims 10 and 18 have been amended to recite similar features).

Applicant notes that portions of the amendments made herein to claims 1, 10, and 18 were previously recited in dependent claim 5, prior to the current amendments. In rejecting dependent claim 5, the Office conceded that Weinert does not disclose or suggest "converting the estimated protein value into a corresponding carbohydrate value using the conversion factor." The Office asserted that Thukral discloses this feature, citing paragraph [0213] and stating that the equations in paragraphs [0200]-[0230] inherently require "a factor." (Office Action, page 6).
Paragraph [0213] of Thukral states "proteins and fat are converted to an equivalent
carbohydrate amount." However, Thukral does not disclose or suggest "converting the estimated

protein value into a corresponding carbohydrate value by applying the estimated protein value to a mathematical function or by dividing the estimated protein value by a conversion factor." Applicant respectfully submits that the equations of paragraphs [0200]-[0230] do not correspond to converting the estimated protein value into a corresponding carbohydrate value, let alone by "applying the estimated protein value to a mathematical function or dividing the estimated protein value by a conversion factor," as recited in Applicant's claims 1, 10, and 18 as amended. Rather, these equations relate to, e.g., an insulin nullified vector (see paragraph [0203]), glucose drop due to insulin utilization (see paragraphs [0206]-[0208]), estimated insulin remaining (see paragraphs [0219]-[0221]), and other parameters that are not related to converting the estimated protein value into a corresponding carbohydrate value.

Applicant respectfully submits independent claims 1, 10, and 18 are allowable for at least a second reason. In rejecting independent claim 1, the Office conceded Weinert does not disclose or suggest "determining an equivalent carbohydrate value for the meal based on converting the estimated protein value into a corresponding carbohydrate value." However, the Office asserted that Thukral discloses this feature, citing paragraph [0213] of Thukral. (Office Action, page 4). As discussed above, Thukral states "proteins and fat are converted to an equivalent carbohydrate amount," however, Thukral makes no mention of how the equivalent carbohydrate amount is determined. Accordingly, Thukral does not disclose or suggest "determining an equivalent carbohydrate value for the meal by adding the estimated carbohydrate value for the meal to the corresponding carbohydrate value associated with the estimated protein value," as recited in amended claims 1, 10, and 18.

For at least these reasons, Applicant respectfully submits independent claims 1, 10, and 18 are allowable. Moreover, 2-9, 11-17, 19, and 20, each of which depend from one of independent claims 1, 10, or 18 are allowable for at least the same reasons corresponding independent claims 1, 10, and 18 are allowable.
For at least these reasons, applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections of the claims under 35 U.S.C. § 103.

The remarks presented herein are fully responsive to the Office Action and are sufficient to overcome the rejections presented in the Office Action. Applicant requests withdrawal of the instant rejections and issuance of a Notice of Allowance. Should any issues remain outstanding, the Examiner is urged to telephone the undersigned to expedite prosecution.
